title: Demand check: meal kits
problem: Is there enough public interest in meal kits among English-speaking readers to justify building a new meal-kit subscription product?
answer: Interest is moderate: meal kits get about 283 views a day on English Wikipedia (high reliability). That is enough to show a real audience, but not a mass-market one.
analysis: Meal kits get about 283 views a day (110,087 over 12 months), in the moderate band (50 to 500 a day).
The level is steady: no single spike drives the total, so this is everyday interest rather than a news event.
conclusions: There is a stable, existing audience that reads about meal kits, so the category is not dead or purely hype-driven.
Moderate interest points to a niche you would need to win share in, not an untapped mass market.
trust: All results are high reliability: full data coverage, enough volume, no spikes, no fetch errors.
Pageviews measure attention, not purchase intent: people may read about meal kits without wanting to buy one.
Only English Wikipedia readers are covered; other languages and markets were not measured.
recommendations: Treat the category as a viable niche: validate willingness to pay with a landing page or pre-orders before building.
Look for a sharper angle (a diet, a price point, an audience) instead of competing head-on as a general meal kit.
Re-run the analysis with competitor brands as separate subjects once share of voice is available.
not_measured: Whether interest is growing or falling (growth_rate is not available yet).
How meal kits compare with alternatives such as grocery delivery (share_of_voice is not available yet).
